mechanism_narrative: A consistently low federal funds rate (below 4.0%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. This signal is always active without threshold conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A labor market tightness indicator (UNRATE above 4.5%) signals high inflationary pressure and potential central bank tightening, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of periods when UNRATE > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST below 1300) and retail sales (RSAFS below 700000) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of periods when HOUST < 1300 and RSAFS < 700000.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS above 4.5%), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher discount rates and reduced corporate investment, with the signal active only in this regime.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year CPI increase above 3.5% (CPIAUCSL > 325) signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to maintain restrictive policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 325.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.5%) and elevated interest rates (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) indicates a sustained monetary tightening cycle, compressing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.5% and FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Strong labor market conditions (PAYEMS above 160000) signal robust consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 40% of periods when PAYEMS > 160000.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, a decline in housing starts (HOUST below 1300) signals potential economic slowdown, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through reduced consumer confidence and investment.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of periods when HOUST < 1300 and economy is in late-cycle expansion.
